text:
Plantando Semillas Community Center / Taller ACÁ

title: Comporta House / Aurora Arquitectos
text:
Comporta House / Aurora Arquitectos

The house is located in the village of Carvalhal, on the Alentejo coast in southern Portugal. Here, long sandy beaches extend inland into flat pine-forested terrain. Those who come here to live or vacation are seeking silence.

title: CST #185  / tini + delavegacanolasso
text:
CST #185 / tini + delavegacanolasso

This project revives the spirit of the Case Study Houses and mid-century modern architecture through an industrialized, optimized system developed with a deep sensitivity to the land.

title: Casa Fogo / Pablo Patriota Arquitetos Associados
text:
Casa Fogo / Pablo Patriota Arquitetos Associados

The most challenging lots are my best friends. In my view of the design craft, challenges naturally lead to solutions. The difficult topography of the terrain in Serra Negra, in Bezerros, Pernambuco, the giant boulder embedded in it, the trees that had to be preserved, the clearing where I could place the construction, and the best views all guided how the project should take shape.

title: Freedom Mobile Arch Amphitheatre / Revery Architecture
text:
Freedom Mobile Arch Amphitheatre / Revery Architecture

Framing views of Vancouver's North Shore Mountains, the Freedom Mobile Arch is an open-air amphitheatre designed to remain connected to its surrounding landscape. A sweeping mass-timber canopy shelters audiences of up to 10,000 while preserving the experience of being outdoors. Permanent infrastructure and adaptable seating allow the venue to accommodate performances and gatherings at a wide range of scales.

title: Danubio Budapest Building / T2.a Architects
text:
Danubio Budapest Building / T2.a Architects

Designed by T2a Architects and completed recently on the site of a former river gravel pit on the banks of the Danube in Budapest, the Danubio residential building responds to the unique urban and natural environment, partially overriding the rules of Budapest real estate developers, and realizes a concept that treats sustainability not only as a slogan but also revives many pre-existing but now forgotten architectural solutions and recreates them in a modern, timeless form.

title: Planá Kindergarten  / PROAM ARCHITEKTI
text:
Planá Kindergarten / PROAM ARCHITEKTI

The new municipal kindergarten in Planá, South Bohemia, represents a sensitive yet confident introduction of modern architecture into a historic rural setting. A sustainable public building made of timber has been created on a small but visually prominent site. Its form immediately reveals its purpose—a building for children that is part traditional, part modern, and somewhat fairytale-like.

title: Building from Place: Inside the Work of RAMA Estudio
text:
Building from Place: Inside the Work of RAMA Estudio

Carla Chávez, Carolina Rodas, and Felipe Donoso began collaborating while studying architecture in Quito, Ecuador, and went on to found RAMA Estudio, one of the winners of the ArchDaily Next Practices Awards 2026. For more than a decade, their practice has moved between housing, public spaces, adaptive reuse, and community initiatives. Their work is guided by an understanding of architecture as a service. For them, a project begins with the circumstances of a place and extends to the people who will build it and those who will live with it for years.

title: Gamaya Farms / Biome Environmental Solutions
text:
Gamaya Farms / Biome Environmental Solutions

Gamaya Farms redefines architectural iconism not through bold geometry, but through absolute camouflage and tectonic erasure. Situated near Vikarabad, along a forested plateau and rolling hills, the project serves as a shared amenities zone and eco-resort for a farm-plot community. Rather than treating the program as a monolithic footprint, the master plan deconstructs the traditional resort layout into distinct, site-specific architectural typologies.

title: Sumayya Vally Unveils First Permanent UAE Project With Dubai’s Elie Khouri Art Foundation
text:
Sumayya Vally Unveils First Permanent UAE Project With Dubai’s Elie Khouri Art Foundation

The Elie Khouri Art Foundation (EKAF) has appointed Sumayya Vally of Johannesburg- and London-based practice Counterspace to design its permanent home in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. Scheduled to open in late 2028, the institution will occupy a repurposed villa in the Jumeirah 1 district, transforming the existing residential property and its surrounding grounds into a space for contemporary art exhibitions, education, and public programming. The appointment forms part of EKAF's plans to establish a permanent platform for contemporary art in Dubai, with architecture and curatorial programming developed in parallel.

title: Cultural and Community Center Stara Fužina / OFIS Architects
text:
Cultural and Community Center Stara Fužina / OFIS Architects

A HOUSE BUILT BY ITS COMMUNITY Villagers and the wider local community built the cultural center in Stara Fužina in 1983 through contributions of income, materials, knowledge, and labor. The need for a shared cultural space dates back to the years after the Second World War, when the village created a temporary hall and stage in the former Zois manor. The new cultural center later provided a permanent setting for events, gatherings, and public life. Its significance therefore comes not only from the building itself, but also from the way the community created and used it over several decades. The renovation continues this principle. The existing house remains the framework for collective activity while adapting to contemporary forms of work, gathering, and cultural production.

title: Egypt’s New Administrative Capital Through the Lens of Manuel Álvarez Diestro
text:
Egypt’s New Administrative Capital Through the Lens of Manuel Álvarez Diestro

Egypt's New Administrative Capital (NAC), located about 45 kilometers east of Cairo, is one of two major urban development projects under construction near the Egyptian capital, along with New Cairo, a satellite city east of Cairo's Ring Road that dates back to the 2000s. To date, Cairo remains the official capital of the country, but various government functions have been moved to the purpose-built city. The new capital in Egypt's Eastern Desert recalls the iconic modernist initiative of Brasília and adds to similar recent projects in countries such as Equatorial Guinea, Indonesia and South Korea. Manuel Álvarez Diestro's photographic work offers a glimpse of this endeavor from the perspective of a pedestrian approaching the urban landscape.

title: Reading the City from Above: Drone Imagery and the Material Layers of Urban Environments
text:
Reading the City from Above: Drone Imagery and the Material Layers of Urban Environments

Beyond their buildings, infrastructure, and streets, cities can be understood as territories shaped by materials, resources, and processes of transformation that define their physical environments. As drone technology becomes increasingly integrated into architectural documentation and urban analysis, aerial imagery offers new opportunities to examine these different layers at multiple scales. As Jane Jacobs once suggested, "Cities are the mines of the future."

title: RHR House / Three Sixty Architecture
text:
RHR House / Three Sixty Architecture

Drawing ideas from place and environment through materials and color palette, RHR House has an initial composition that is brutal but simple, reminiscent of a boat moored next to a wharf. The arrival is one of slow reveal, with pauses in time; following a timber boardwalk, you are drawn to a soft green stair form floating from the concrete floor above. This leads upwards to the entry door, semi-concealed and casual, as you would find in a seaside Bach.

title: Pusayapuri Housing / EKAR
text:
Pusayapuri Housing / EKAR

Unlike Sukhothai and Ayutthaya, U Thong is a forgotten city, even though it holds one of the oldest civilizations in Thailand. Almost no tangible evidence remains to show Thai people how old the city really is. What is left are the bases of collapsed pagodas scattered across the area and tiny beads found in the soil. The people of U Thong have collected these objects for almost a hundred years and once came together to set up a museum, but there was not enough to tell the story of the city.

title: Ocaso House / JE arquitectos + Leo Alvarez
text:
Ocaso House / JE arquitectos + Leo Alvarez

Located in Chelem, Yucatán, Casa Ocaso emerges from the convergence of two conditions: a constantly transforming coastline and the decision of three friends to share a home without sacrificing their privacy.

title: FR House / N.2B Arquitetura
text:
FR House / N.2B Arquitetura

The FR House transforms the challenges of a corner lot into an architecture that reveals itself gradually, exploring the relationship between light, nature, materiality, and spatial experience.

title: Casa Nostra Kindergarten / Sarquella Torres
text:
Casa Nostra Kindergarten / Sarquella Torres

Set on the southern edge of Banyoles Lake, La finca de Casa Nostra occupies a site of exceptional environmental sensitivity. Acquired in 1926 by Magdalena Aulina's Cultural Institution, the property has supported educational activities for nearly a century. Over time, these have accumulated in the form of a small campus, a constellation of buildings constructed incrementally and shaped by the landscape as much as by institutional need.

title: Benfica AM & MR Villa / João Tiago Aguiar, Arquitectos
text:
Benfica AM & MR Villa / João Tiago Aguiar, Arquitectos

The intervention in this house in Benfica, set close to the surrounding woodland is based on a strategy of continuity and transformation. The original construction is partially preserved through the retention of the main façade and part of the lateral elevation, maintaining its urban presence and memory, while the intervention focuses on extending the house over the rear garden, fully redesigning the rear elevation.

title: Downtown Cary Park / Machado Silvetti
text:
Downtown Cary Park / Machado Silvetti

Downtown Cary Park is the centerpiece of an investment by the citizens of the Town of Cary in enhancing, expanding, and protecting the public life of their rapidly growing community. Located in the heart of downtown Cary, North Carolina, the park is a transformational synthesis of urban design, landscape, architecture, and programming that benefits the local community and the greater region.

title: Viking Fortress Borgring Experience Center / LOOP Architects
text:
Viking Fortress Borgring Experience Center / LOOP Architects

At the Viking Fortress Borgring, history and landscape are brought to life through an experience center inspired by the Viking Age's characteristic longhouses and royal halls. The experience center is designed by LOOP Architects, with LYTT Architecture and engineering firm VIGGO MADSEN as sub-consultants.

title: Bridge House / Studioshaw
text:
Bridge House / Studioshaw

Studioshaw announces the completion of Bridge House, an eight-story, 6,250 sqm mixed-use development at the heart of Hackney Wick. Delivering 40 apartments alongside dual-level commercial and community spaces, and set beside a new public square, the project marks the practice's largest scheme to date. Its completion coincides with Studioshaw's tenth anniversary and the delivery of its 100th project.

title: Archohm: Indian Contemporary Architecture
text:
Archohm: Indian Contemporary Architecture

This publication compiles 25 years of work by Studio Archohm, highlighting their evolution into key players in Indian nation-building through large-scale urban, infrastructure, and civic projects, alongside private-sector experimentation.
The studio's multidisciplinary portfolio spans design research, city branding, education, and experience design, connecting scales from small objects to entire master plans. The featured projects seek to unlock space potential while balancing indigenous practices with global perspectives to reimagine a contemporary Indian design identity. title: TC 177/78- João Mendes Ribeiro
text:
TC 177/78- João Mendes Ribeiro

This double issue brings together, across 406 pages, twenty-five years of work by the Portuguese architect João Mendes Ribeiro (Coimbra, 1960) through eighteen works built in Portugal and Spain between 2000 and 2026. Trained in Porto and assistant to Fernando Távora in Coimbra during the 1990s, Mendes Ribeiro has developed a singular career in which architecture, theatre set design and the design of objects and interiors feed into one another.
